idiom_name: return the error at the first failure (if err != nil) + panic only for unrecoverable states
implementation_notes: Go has no exceptions, so fail-fast is a local discipline: check every error at the point it appears and return immediately, which is the shape the standard library and the Go blog present as normal code. Functions that cannot produce a value return it together with an error, callers propagate with one guard line, and classification uses errors.Is / errors.As rather than message matching; defer releases what the attempt acquired on both paths. panic/recover exists but is reserved for unrecoverable states or bugs inside a package - the standard library does use it internally and converts it to an error at its boundary, which is the pattern for libraries that must not crash their host.
pitfalls: A returned error that a caller drops with _ or only logs reintroduces fail-slow behaviour; nothing in the language forces the check.
panic unwinds only the current goroutine and only through its deferred calls: recovering in a library swallows a bug, while panicking in a handler kills the process.
Wrapping loses the ability to classify unless the cause stays inspectable (%w); string-matching error messages breaks as soon as a message changes.
